title: Rye & Spelt Kefir Loaf (1.2 kg)
subtitle: Technical Baking Sheet
scalingPrinciple: Item A.01 (Total Flour Base) is locked at 100.0% in the baker's convention — the sum of all rye and spelt flour across both the levain and the final dough. Every liquid, salt, and yeast figure reads as a true baker's percentage against that 650 g flour mass.

rows.name: Total Flour Base (Rye + Spelt)
rows.role: Combined flour mass; the baker's-percentage reference for the whole formula.

rows.name: Organic Whole Rye Flour (levain)
rows.role: Levain flour; drawn from the total flour base.

rows.name: Milk Kefir (room temperature)
rows.role: Wild culture and acid source; drives the 12-hour levain.

rows.name: Organic Whole Rye Flour (final)
rows.role: Brings total rye to 325 g (50% of flour base).

rows.name: Whole Spelt Flour
rows.role: Provides the extensibility rye cannot; balances the crumb.

rows.name: Warm Water (32°C)
rows.role: Adjusted downward to account for the kefir's own hydration.

rows.name: Instant Yeast
rows.role: Insurance leavening; ensures a dense mass of rye and spelt expands before the crust sets.

rows.name: Miso (optional)
rows.role: Optional umami depth; whisked into the liquids.

total.role: Combined raw material input footprint — the 1.2 kg target loaf.

matrixFootnote: *Miso is given as 1 tbsp in the source; the gram value is a standard culinary conversion and is marked accordingly. Note that B.01 and C.01/C.02 are components of the A.01 flour baseline, not additions to it — the flour is listed once as a total and again as its split between levain and final dough.

mise.label: The 12-Hour Kefir Levain (B.01, B.02)
mise.text: Mix 150 g organic whole rye flour with 150 g room-temperature milk kefir. Let sit at room temperature until active and bubbly — approximately 12 hours.

mise.label: Vessel Check
mise.text: This is a large loaf. If using a Dutch oven, ensure it is at least 5 quarts. If using a loaf pan, a standard 9×5 inch pan is required so the dough does not overflow.

execution.name: The Mix
execution.text: Whisk the water, levain, and miso together. Stir in the flours, salt, and yeast until a thick, sticky paste forms.

execution.name: Bulk Rise
execution.text: Cover and place in a warm spot. Perform one strength fold with wet hands at the 30-minute mark.

execution.name: Shape
execution.text: Transfer to a large, well-greased loaf pan (9×5 inch or similar) or a large banneton. If proofing in a banneton, use excessive rye flour to prevent sticking — rye and spelt are far stickier than standard wheat, and 1,200 g of 80% hydration dough exerts significant pressure.

execution.name: Final Proof
execution.text: Let rise until the dough looks tight and small fissures appear on the surface.

execution.name: Bake — Lid On
execution.text: Bake in a Dutch oven or with steam.

execution.name: Bake — Lid Off
execution.text: Continue until the crust is dark and the internal temperature reaches 98°C.

directive: At 80% hydration and 1,200 g total mass this dough is heavy and slack. Use wet hands for every contact, flour a banneton far past the point that feels excessive, and confirm your vessel is large enough before the bulk rise — there is no recovery from a dough that overflows its pan mid-proof.
